body.statement: The family \(P^{\circ}\), indexed by \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), has an \((X,Z)\)-marginal density bounded and strictly positive on its finite rectangle support and uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies the marginal quasi-stayer part of Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024), while baseline-conditional positivity \(P(|Z|\le\eta\mid X)>0\) fails throughout \([-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The displayed laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) share \(P^{\circ}\), satisfy the source's Assumptions 1--4, including parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, and in fact satisfy the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period difference is dose-invariant. They have different WAOSS values. Therefore the Appendix step immediately before display (4) does not follow from the proceedings paper's marginal Assumption 4.
body.justification: A regular region, rather than a hand-tuned atom, establishes that the support defect has substantive identifying consequences.
body.gap: Theorem 1 of the proceedings paper states identification under Assumptions 1--4, but Assumption 4 is marginal and its Appendix proof invokes stronger baseline-conditional positivity immediately before display (4). The explicit conditional support regime in arXiv:2201.06898v1 handles the point-identified case, not the full-law sharp set on the positive-mass failure region exhibited here.
body.consumer: Users of the published WAOSS estimator obtain an exact support diagnostic identifying when its nonparametric formula remains justified.
body.proof_tex:
Under \(P^{\circ}\), the first rectangle has area \(1/2\) and density \(2p_{\circ}\), hence mass \(p_{\circ}\); the second has area \(1/2\) and density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\), hence mass \(1-p_{\circ}\).  Both densities are finite and strictly positive because \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\).  The outcomes vanish and are therefore uniformly bounded.  Absolute continuity gives \(P^{\circ}(Z=0)=0\).  On the second rectangle, every neighborhood of zero in the \(z\)-coordinate has positive probability, so
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta)>0\qquad\text{for every }\eta>0.
\]
This is the source's marginal quasi-stayer requirement.  In contrast, for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), the conditional support of \(Z\) is \([1/2,1]\), and hence
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta\mid X=x)=0
\qquad(0<\eta<1/2).
\]
Since the first rectangle has mass \(p_{\circ}\), the failure region has precisely that baseline probability.

For either sign \(s\in\{+,-\}\), the definition gives, outside the null event \(Z=0\),
\[
Y_2^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)=u_s^{\circ}(X)
\qquad\text{for every }d\in[-2,2].
\]
Thus the schedules are static, their period difference has conditional mean \(u_s^{\circ}(X)\) given either \((X,Z)\) or \(X\), and parallel trends holds on the baseline support and indeed on all of \(I\).  At the observed doses,
\[
Y_1^{Q_s^{\circ}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_s^{\circ}}(D_2)=0=Y_2,
\]
so both laws match the full observed law.  The function \(u_s^{\circ}\) is bounded by one and is one-Lipschitz.  On \([-1,0]\), \(|u_s^{\circ}(X)|\leq1/2\leq Z\), while on \([0,1]\) it vanishes.  Therefore each schedule slope \(-u_s^{\circ}(X)/Z\) is bounded in absolute value by one, which proves latent integrability on compact \(I\) and the conditional mean-movement bound.  These verifications establish the substantive staticity, consistency, support, slope, and parallel-trends clauses invoked from the source's Assumptions 1--4.

The signed baseline measure is supported only by the first rectangle because \(S=1\) there and the conditional sign mean is zero on the symmetric second rectangle.  Hence
\[
d\nu_{P^{\circ}}(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx.
\]
Also \(T=0\), and
\[
A=p_{\circ}\frac34+(1-p_{\circ})\frac18
=\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8.
\]
Since
\[
\int_{-1}^0\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx=\frac38,
\]
the two completions have
\[
\theta(Q_+^{\circ})=-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\qquad
\theta(Q_-^{\circ})=\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}.
\]
They share the same observed law but have different WAOSS values.  Thus marginal quasi-stayers cannot imply the baseline-conditional positivity used immediately before the cited display, and cannot by themselves identify the asserted singleton.
